findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden (a child's FAILs: `_fail_scope(v, holders[0], s["seq"], s["stepId"])`) and _tainted (`or s["stepId"] == repairer`); README 'A FAIL crosses the delegation boundary both ways', second bullet ('the delegation itself, which carries the child's repair, is not covered')
findings.finding:
The R7-1 exemption is keyed to the deciding delegation alone, and it skips that delegation entirely. That is too wide on one side and too narrow on the other.
(1) Too wide (K803d). m2 builds N on patch (X). A delegation consumes patch; its child's unit-tests FAILs X, and the child, revising nothing, delivers a fresh N that only schema-check passed. The parent writes the delegation's N and delivers a final step built on the write. Accepted. The same steps in one loop are refused (K803e), and so is the same parent with the FAIL decided in the parent (K803f: the delegation repeats covered bytes). The delegation carried no repair, and N reached a write that the gate that failed never checked. K803 (the child revises X to N, which passes unit-tests) is accepted too, while one loop refuses it (K803c: a revision returns bytes the FAIL covers).
(2) Too narrow, and new in round 8 (K820). d1 consumes patch (X); its child FAILs X and repairs it (Y passes unit-tests). d2, consuming nothing, runs a child that regenerates X and FAILs it again. The parent builds its answer on d1. Refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN: under d2's FAIL, d1 is an ordinary consumer of patch. Round 7 accepts it, and so does the same loop in one trace (K820c: a revision of the artefact is never covered).
The README states neither case.

findings.location: README 'Not claimed' ('FAILs across loops beyond the rules above') and 'A FAIL crosses the delegation boundary both ways'
findings.finding:
The new 'Not claimed' bullet names three residuals, all of a parent's FAIL reaching into a child. The child-to-parent direction has its own, which it does not name. Each is accepted, while the same steps in one loop are refused:
- C801, a later sibling. The parent hands patch (X) to d1, whose child FAILs X and repairs it. d2 (consuming nothing) runs a child that regenerates X, gates it with schema-check only and writes it (C801c refused). 'Crosses one delegation boundary' implies the limit, but the parent holds X and the FAIL is decided in its record. C801b (the parent never holds X) is accepted as well.
- K823, the mirror of C702. A child derives N from X before its FAIL of X; after the delegation the parent regenerates N and writes it (K823c refused).
- K824, the mirror of C703. A child's revision Y passes schema-check only (unit-tests failed X) and is not used; the parent regenerates Y and writes it (K824c refused).
findings.requiredChange:
Name these under 'Not claimed': a child's FAIL does not reach a later sibling, bytes the child derived, or the child's unverified revision bytes regenerated in the parent. Or close the sibling case.
